headline: GOTECH opens in Dubai with 93 sessions and an oil company plenary
deck: SPE's Dubai showcase runs five concurrent rooms across three days, with EGPC, ADNOC Onshore and Offshore, Dragon Oil and Sharjah National Oil on the opening panel.
excerpt: GOTECH opens at Dubai World Trade Centre on 29 September with 93 sessions across five concurrent rooms and a chief executive plenary drawn from regional national oil companies.
content:
GOTECH, the Society of Petroleum Engineers' gas and oil technology showcase, runs at Dubai World Trade Centre from 29 September to 1 October with a technical programme of 93 sessions: seven panel and plenary sessions, 52 technical sessions, 19 poster sessions and an opening ceremony, across five concurrent rooms.

The chief executive plenary is drawn from regional operators rather than from service companies — the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation, ADNOC Onshore and ADNOC Offshore, OiLSERV Kuwait, Dragon Oil, Sharjah National Oil Corporation and United Energy Group, moderated by Carole Nakhle, chief executive of Crystol Energy. Jennifer Miskimins, the SPE's 2026 president, is confirmed, as is Faye Gerard of the International Association of Oil and Gas Producers. Baker Hughes, SLB and Halliburton appear on the programme.

The declared tracks say something about where the regional technical conversation has moved. Artificial intelligence and digital applications for reservoir and production management lead; mature fields and marginal assets follow; then drilling, completions and well integrity; carbon capture, utilisation and storage; talent; and nanotechnology.

Mature fields and marginal assets is the track worth watching. The Gulf's producing assets are, in several cases, decades into their lives, and the engineering problem is shifting from developing new capacity toward sustaining recovery from reservoirs that are watering out. That is a different discipline with a different economics — incremental barrels from existing infrastructure, where the capital test is far tighter than for a greenfield development, and where the decision to continue is taken repeatedly rather than once. It connects directly to the asset integrity questions covered at STATIC Arabia in Al Khobar earlier this month: a field being produced beyond its original design life is served by surface facilities in the same position.

CCUS as a standing track reflects commitments already made rather than aspiration. This publication has reported QatarEnergy awarding Samsung C&T a 4.1 million tonne carbon capture project at Ras Laffan, and ADNOC's broader programme; those projects create a technical community that needs somewhere to compare notes.

The event's timing has moved. Older listings place GOTECH in April 2026, while SPE's own programme page carries the September and October dates. No reason for the change has been published by the organiser, and none should be inferred.

For the Gulf supply chain, an SPE technical conference is a different proposition from a trade exhibition: the audience is engineers evaluating methods rather than buyers evaluating products, and the commercial return is measured in specification influence rather than in orders taken on the floor. SPE technical programmes are peer-reviewed, which makes the session list a reasonable proxy for what Gulf operators are actually working on.
author: Jakson Gudawela
